meta.maintainer: EHL SBP Group 36 until hand-over; after that the list needs a named owner at HFTP
meta.note: A dated, sourced change log, not a news feed. Add an entry only after checking it at the source. 'affects' links each entry to tools in a register: basis (labels resting on that kind of source), uses (use-case ids), depts, labels, packs, roles, countries or all.

entries.title: Final Commission guidelines on high-risk AI
entries.what: The Commission's guidelines on which uses count as high-risk exist only as a draft of 19 May 2026. The final version is due by the end of 2026.
entries.why: It could change the 'High-risk if…' labels for rotas, housekeeping tools, voice agents, cameras and face check-in. Re-check every label marked 'Draft guidance' when it appears.
entries.source: European Commission, draft guidelines on the classification of high-risk AI systems (19 May 2026) and consultation page; booklet, What is still moving

entries.title: Two new bans apply: AI-made intimate images and child sexual abuse material
entries.what: The July 2026 amendment added two prohibited practices to Article 5. They apply from 2 Dec 2026.
entries.why: For hotels this concerns misuse of image tools by staff. It is one more reason to give staff approved tools and an AI-use policy.

entries.title: Marking deadline for older AI content generators
entries.what: Image, audio, video and text generators placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026 must mark their output as AI-made in a machine-readable way by 2 Dec 2026.
entries.why: It matters to a group that built or adapted its own generator. Hotels that use a vendor's generator can ask the vendor to confirm.

entries.title: New product liability rules apply
entries.what: AI that a group builds for its own use and puts into use after 9 Dec 2026 counts as a product it manufactures. EU countries must bring the rules into national law; Germany has done so.
entries.why: A group that builds its own tools answers for defects without proof of fault, and courts can order it to disclose design records. Hotels that only use vendor tools are not manufacturers.
entries.source: Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853; booklet A3, A8

entries.title: Commission guidelines on who is the maker along the value chain
entries.what: Guidelines on Article 25, which decides when a user becomes the maker of a high-risk tool, are announced but not yet published.
entries.why: They should settle the least clear point for hotels: whether staff using a general chatbot to rank applicants makes the hotel the tool's maker.
entries.source: Project data file (ai-act-data.json), open items; desk research 17 Nov 2026

entries.title: Possible lighter rules for AI in regulated products
entries.what: The July 2026 amendment lets the Commission limit the high-risk requirements for AI in products already covered by EU safety law. It must adopt the detail by 2 Aug 2027.
entries.why: It affects AI in lifts, gas appliances and pressure equipment. Until then, assume no relief.
entries.source: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art. 2(13); project revision list of 10 Nov 2026

entries.title: High-risk rules start for staff tools and biometrics
entries.what: From this date the duties for high-risk AI apply to recruiting, staff ranking and monitoring tools and to biometric tools.
entries.why: Vendors must have CE-marked and registered their tools; hotels must use them under trained human oversight, keep logs and inform staff.
entries.source: AI Act Art. 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

entries.title: Cyber Resilience Act duties for connected products
entries.what: Connected products sold to hotels must meet the Cyber Resilience Act from 11 Dec 2027.
entries.why: Ask makers of robots, smart kitchen equipment and other connected devices for proof of conformity when buying.
entries.source: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act); booklet A5, C4

entries.title: High-risk rules start for AI in regulated products
entries.what: From this date the high-risk rules apply to AI that is a safety component of products such as lifts and gas appliances.
entries.why: This is the maker's duty. Hotels ask the maker whether the product carries the CE mark for its AI function.
entries.source: AI Act Art. 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

entries.title: Challenge to the EU–US Data Privacy Framework
entries.what: The framework that lets guest data go to US providers is valid but under challenge at the EU Court of Justice.
entries.why: If it falls, guest data sent to US-hosted AI tools needs another legal basis, and tools without EU hosting may need replacing. Know where each vendor stores data before any ruling.
entries.source: Booklet B1, What is still moving

entries.title: Digital Fairness Act proposal
entries.what: The Commission's proposal would ban persistent scarcity prompts during booking and profiling-based prices likely to harm guests known to be minors or vulnerable. It would apply 12 months after it becomes law.
entries.why: It would add rules for pricing, upselling and booking-engine tools on top of today's consumer law.
entries.source: Booklet C3, What is still moving

entries.title: A possible EU law on AI at work
entries.what: The European Parliament has asked the Commission for rules on algorithmic management of workers.
entries.why: It would add duties for tools that assign, schedule, monitor or evaluate staff.

entries.title: Proposed changes to the GDPR
entries.what: The Commission has proposed changes to data protection law, including on using personal data for AI.
entries.why: It could change what vendors may do with guest and staff data.

entries.title: National authorities and penalty laws
entries.what: Each EU country names its own AI Act authorities and sets its own penalty rules. Germany's law has been in force since 29 July 2026; France's is still before parliament; Spain has no implementing law; Sweden's authority acts under an interim mandate to 31 Dec 2026.
entries.why: It decides who would contact a hotel and what a breach costs in that country. Your country's status is on the 'Your hotel' tab where the project has researched it.
entries.source: Project data file (ai-act-data.json), national layer, researched November 2026

entries.title: Swiss AI bill
entries.what: The Federal Council plans to open consultation on an AI bill in spring 2027.
entries.why: Until then the Swiss Data Protection Act and labour law apply to AI directly.
entries.source: Booklet D1, What is still moving

entries.title: UK: the regulator's AI code and guidance on automated decisions
entries.what: The data protection regulator must publish a code on AI and final guidance on decisions made by machine alone. A Cyber Security and Resilience Bill is before Parliament.
entries.why: They will set what UK hotels must do on AI decisions and cyber security.
entries.source: Booklet D2, What is still moving
